title: Activation of emulsion polymerisation by a hydrocarbon‐soluble vanadium compound
abstract: AbstractA hydrocarbon‐soluble vanadium‐activated system consisting essentially of vanadyl di‐isopropylsalicylate and phenylcyclohexane hydroperoxide proved to be an active initiation system for the low‐temperature emulsion copolymerisation of butadiene and styrene. Mercaptans were observed to have a promoting as well as a modifying effect in this system. Whereas complete omission of the mercaptan resulted in a very low conversion, high conversions were obtained with as little as 0‐01 g per 100 g of monomer. No initiation took place when the polymerisation was carried out in a homogeneous phase, e.g. in benzene.
